questions.q: Why does this lesson say a health check that just prints to a console still leaves the original problem unsolved?
options: Because console output is technically impossible in PowerShell
Because consoles cannot run on a schedule
Because someone still has to remember to go look at the output — the exact same manual-dependency gap as before
Because the health check itself would fail without alerting
questions.explain: Alerting is specifically about removing the need for a human to manually check — a silent, unwatched check doesn't do that.

questions.q: What does Send-OverlookAlert actually do in this lesson's example?
options: Sends an email via Send-MailMessage to the on-call DBA's address when a check fails
Automatically fixes the failed condition
Deletes the failed database
Restores the database from backup automatically
questions.explain: The mechanism is deliberately simple: a failed condition triggers an automatic email to a specific on-call address.

questions.q: How does this lesson wire Lesson 17's and Lesson 18's work into the alerting script?
options: It replaces both checks with a single Azure Portal setting
It rewrites both checks from scratch
It ignores both and only checks database uptime
It calls Test-OverlookHealth and Test-OverlookBackup, and sends an alert specifically when OverallHealthy or BackupVerified comes back false
questions.explain: The alerting script reuses the two prior functions directly, checking their summary flags to decide whether to notify.

questions.q: What specifically does this lesson say closes Lesson 1's 'whoever happened to be on call' problem?
options: The checks running whether or not any specific person is thinking about them, and the alert reaching whoever is actually on call, not whoever built the script
Moving the database to a different region
Deleting the on-call rotation entirely
Hiring more DBA staff
questions.explain: This is the direct technical answer to the informal, person-dependent access and process problem named in Lesson 1.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's a more sophisticated real-world alternative to Send-MailMessage mentioned as context?
options: Azure Monitor action groups or a paging service, using the same underlying mechanism of a failed condition automatically triggering a notification
There is no alternative; email is the only option
A second database replica
A manual phone tree with no automation
questions.explain: The lesson keeps the example simple but notes that larger environments might use action groups or paging — the mechanism is the same.
